summary: S. 2016 authorizes and directs a land exchange between the Chugach Alaska Corporation and the federal government. Under the bill, if the corporation offers to convey roughly 231,000 acres of subsurface estate to the Department of the Interior within one year, the federal government must exchange it for approximately 65,374 acres of fee simple land located in the Chugach region.

affected_groups.effect: Must offer approximately 231,000 acres of subsurface estate within one year to receive about 65,374 acres of federal fee simple land in exchange.
Must accept the offered subsurface estate, execute the land exchange, and consolidate federal ownership of surface and subsurface estates under the Exxon Valdez program.
affected_groups.group: Federal Government (Department of the Interior, Forest Service, Bureau of Land Management, and National Park Service)

key_provisions: Directs the Secretary of the Interior to accept about 231,000 acres of subsurface estate from the Chugach Alaska Corporation if offered within one year of the bill's enactment.
Requires the federal government to convey approximately 65,374 acres of fee simple land (including National Forest System, Bureau of Land Management, and National Park Service lands) in exchange.

Excludes from the corporation's conveyance any lands up to a total of 209 acres where a village corporation retains non-timber development rights or has designated land for a shareholder homesite program.
Allows the Secretary and the corporation to correct minor errors in maps, acreage estimates, or land descriptions by mutual agreement, with maps controlling in the event of a conflict.
Maintains valid existing rights, reservations, rights-of-way, and third-party encumbrances on the exchanged lands.
missing_information: Long-term economic costs or administrative expenses for the Department of the Interior to complete the land transfers.
Specific details on the exact valuation or monetary equivalence of the subsurface and surface lands being exchanged.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 2016 authorizes and directs a land exchange between the Chugach Alaska Corporation and the federal government. Under the bill, if the corporation offers to convey roughly 231,000 acres of subsurface estate to the Department of the Interior within one year, the federal government must exchange it for approximately 65,374 acres of fee simple land located in the Chugach region.
summary_detail.significance: The bill addresses split estate ownership conflicts resulting from past conservation acquisitions following the Exxon Valdez oil spill. It consolidates federal surface and subsurface ownership while transferring roughly 65,374 acres of federal land to the Chugach Alaska Corporation.
